blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Keeping the water away

New approaches to flood control

A Recently, winter floods on the rivers of central Europe have been among the worst for 600 to 700 years, and dams and dykes (protective sea walls) have failed to solve the problem. Traditionally, river engineers have tried to get rid of the water quickly, draining it off the land and down to the sea in rivers reengineered as high-performance drains. But however high they build the artificial riverbanks, the floods keep coming back. And when they come, they seem to be worse than ever.

B Engineers are now turning to a different plan: to sap the water's destructive strength by dispersing it into fields, forgotten lakes and flood plains. They are reviving river bends and marshes to curb the flow, and even plugging city drains to encourage floodwater to use other means to go underground. Back in the days when rivers took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume while meandering across flood plains and inland deltas, but today the water tends to have a direct passage to the sea. This means that, when it rains in the uplands, the water comes down all at once.

C Worse, when the flood plains are closed off, the river's flow downstream becomes more violent and uncontrollable; by turning complex river systems into the simple mechanics of a water pipe, engineers have often created danger where they promised safety. The Rhine, Europe's most engineered river, is a good example. For a long time engineers have erased its backwaters and cut it off from its plain. The aim was partly to improve navigation, and partly to speed floodwaters out of the Alps and down to the North Sea. Now, when it rains in the Alps, the peak flows from several branches of the Rhine coincide where once they arrived separately, and with four-fifths of the Lower Rhine's flood plain barricaded off, the waters rise. The result is more frequent flooding and greater damage. The same thing has happened in the US on the Mississippi River, which drains the world's second-largest river catchment into the Gulf of Mexico. Despite some $7 billion spent over the last century on levees (embankments), the situation is growing worse.

D Specialists in water control now say that a new approach is needed — one which takes the whole landscape into consideration. To help keep London's feet dry, the UK Environment Agency is reflooding 10 square kilometres of the ancient flood plain of the River Thames outside Oxford. Nearer to London, it has spent £100 million creating new wetlands and a relief channel across 16 kilometres of flood plain. Similar ideas are being tested in Austria, in one of Europe's largest river restorations to date. The engineers calculate that the restored flood plain of the Drava River can now store up to 10 million cubic metres of floodwater, and slow down storm surges coming out of the Alps by more than an hour, protecting towns not only in Austria, but as far downstream as Slovenia and Croatia.

E The Dutch, for whom preventing floods is a matter of survival, have gone furthest. This nation, built largely on drained marshes and seabed, has had several severe shocks in the last two decades, when very large numbers of people have had to be evacuated. Since that time, the Dutch have broken one of their most enduring national stereotypes by allowing engineers to punch holes in dykes. They plan to return up to a sixth of the country to its former waterlogged state in order to better protect the rest.

F Water use in cities also needs to change. At the moment, cities seem to create floods; they are concreted and paved so that rains flow quickly into rivers. A new breed of ‘soft engineers' wants cities to be porous; Berlin is one place where this is being done. Tough new rules for new developments mean that drains will be prevented from becoming overloaded after heavy rains. Architects of new urban buildings are diverting rainwater from the roofs for use in toilets and the irrigation of roof gardens, while water falling onto the ground is collected in ponds, or passes underground through porous paving. One high-tech urban development can store a sixth of its annual rainfall, and reuse most of the rest.

G Could this be expanded to protect a whole city? The test case could be Los Angeles. With non-porous surfaces covering 70% of the city, drainage is a huge challenge. Billions of dollars have been spent digging huge drains and concreting riverbeds, but many communities still flood regularly. Meanwhile, this desert city ships water from hundreds of kilometres away to fill its taps and swimming pool. Los Angeles has recently launched a new scheme to utilise floodwater in the Sun Valley section of the city. The plan is to catch the rain that falls on thousands of driveways, parking lots and rooftops in the valley. Trees will soak up water from parking lots; houses and public buildings will capture roof water to irrigate gardens and parks, and road drains will empty into old gravel pits to recharge the city's underground water reserves. Result: less flooding and more water for the city. It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities and protect areas from flooding, and how little this method achieves.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–G, in boxes 14–19 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEFG
14 how legislation has forced building designers to improve water use
15 two reasons why one river was isolated from its flood plain
16 how natural watercourses in the past assisted flood control
17 an example of flood control on one river, affecting three countries
18 a country which has partly destroyed one of its most typical features in order to control water
19 the writer's comment on the comparative cost-effectiveness of traditional flood control and newer methods

Questions 20 and 21

Choose TWO letters A–E.

According to the article, which TWO of these statements are true of the new approach to flood control?

Questions 22–26

Complete the sentences below.

Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

22 Some of the most severe floods for many centuries have recently occurred in parts of .

23 The Rhine and the river have experienced similar problems with water control.

24 An area near Oxford will be flooded to protect the city of .

25 Planners who wish to allow water to pass more freely through city surfaces are called .

26 A proposal for part of the city of could show whether small-scale water projects could be applied on a large scale.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 近年来，中欧河流的冬季洪水是600至700年来最严重的，而堤坝未能解决问题。传统上，河流工程师试图快速排除积水，将水从陆地排入大海，把河流改造成高性能排水渠。但无论他们把人工河岸建得多高，洪水总是不断涌来。而且当洪水来临时，它们似乎比以往任何时候都更严重。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 工程师们现在正转向一个不同的计划：通过将水的破坏力分散到田野、被遗忘的湖泊和洪泛区来削弱它。他们正在恢复河湾和沼泽以遏制水流，甚至堵塞城市排水管以鼓励洪水使用其他方式进入地下。在过去河流蜿蜒入海的日子里，洪水在蜿蜒穿过洪泛区和内陆三角洲时失去了力量和水量，但今天的水流往往直接入海。这意味着，当高地降雨时，水会一下子全部涌下来。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 更糟糕的是，当洪泛区被封闭后，河流下游的水流变得更加猛烈和不可控；通过将复杂的河流系统变成简单的水管机械装置，工程师们常常在他们承诺安全的地方制造了危险。欧洲工程化程度最高的河流——莱茵河，就是一个很好的例子。很长一段时间里，工程师们清除了它的回水区，并将其与平原隔离开来。其目的部分是为了改善航运，部分是为了加速洪水从阿尔卑斯山排出并流入北海。现在，当阿尔卑斯山下雨时，莱茵河几个支流的洪峰会同时汇合，而过去它们是分别到达的，并且由于下莱茵河五分之四的洪泛区被隔断，水位上升。结果是更频繁的洪水和更大的损失。同样的事情也发生在美国的密西西比河上，它将世界第二大河流域的水排入墨西哥湾。尽管上个世纪在堤坝（embankments）上花费了约70亿美元，情况却越来越糟。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 水利控制专家现在说，需要一种新方法——一种将整个景观都考虑在内的方法。为了帮助伦敦保持干爽，英国环境署正在牛津外的泰晤斯河古老洪泛区重新淹没10平方公里的土地。在靠近伦敦的地方，它花费了1亿英镑，创建了新的湿地和一个横跨16公里洪泛区的泄洪渠。类似的想法正在奥地利进行测试，这是欧洲迄今为止最大的河流修复项目之一。工程师们计算出，修复后的德拉瓦河洪泛区现在可以储存高达1000万立方米的洪水，并将来自阿尔卑斯山风暴潮的速度减缓一个多小时，不仅保护了奥地利的城镇，还保护了远至下游的斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 对于荷兰人来说，防洪是生死攸关的大事，他们走得最远。这个主要建在排干的沼泽和海床上的国家，在过去二十年中遭受了几次严重的冲击，当时大量人口不得不撤离。从那时起，荷兰人打破了他们最持久的民族定式之一，允许工程师在堤坝上打洞。他们计划将该国多达六分之一的土地恢复到以前被水淹没的状态，以更好地保护其余部分。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 城市的水资源利用也需要改变。目前，城市似乎在制造洪水；它们被混凝土和铺路覆盖，以至于雨水迅速流入河流。一种新型的“软工程师”希望城市变得有渗透性；柏林是正在实践这一理念的地方之一。对新开发的严格新规定意味着，大雨过后，排水管将不会超载。新城市建筑的设计师们正在将屋顶的雨水引流用于厕所和屋顶花园的灌溉，而落在地面上的水则被收集在池塘中，或通过透水铺装渗入地下。一个高科技的城市开发项目可以储存其年降雨量的六分之一，并重复使用其余大部分。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 这能否扩展到保护整个城市？试验案例可能是洛杉矶。由于不透水表面覆盖了城市70%的面积，排水是一个巨大的挑战。尽管花费了数十亿美元挖掘巨大的排水渠和用混凝土浇筑河床，但许多社区仍然经常被淹。与此同时，这个沙漠城市从数百公里外运水来填充其水龙头和游泳池。洛杉矶最近启动了一项新计划，以利用该市太阳谷地区的洪水。该计划是收集落在山谷中成千上万的车道、停车场和屋顶上的雨水。树木将吸收停车场的雨水；房屋和公共建筑将收集屋顶雨水来灌溉花园和公园，道路排水管将排入旧的砾石坑，以补充城市的地下水储备。结果是：更少的洪水和更多的城市用水。这听起来可能很昂贵，直到我们意识到为了排干城市和保护地区免受洪水侵袭花费了多少钱，以及这种方法收效甚微。

items.text:
(1) 题目 14：how legislation has forced building designers to improve water use （法律如何迫使建筑设计师改进城市用水）
答案：F
解析：F段提到“Tough new rules for new developments...”（对新开发的严格新规），这即是“legislation”（立法），并具体说明了建筑师如何被要求“diverting rainwater...”（引流雨水），这正是改进用水的措施。

(2) 题目 15：two reasons why one river was isolated from its flood plain （说明某条河为何与其洪泛平原隔离的两个原因）
答案：C
解析：C段明确给出了莱茵河被改造的两个原因：“The aim was partly to improve navigation, and partly to speed floodwaters...”。

(3) 题目 16：how natural watercourses in the past assisted flood control （过去的自然水路如何帮助防洪）
答案：B
解析：B段描述了过去河流“took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume while meandering across flood plains...”，解释了自然蜿蜒的水道如何通过减缓水流和分散水量来帮助控制洪水。

(4) 题目 17：an example of flood control on one river, affecting three countries （在一条河上实施的防洪实例，其影响波及三个国家）
答案：D
解析：D段提到了德拉瓦河（Drava River）的修复项目，并明确指出其保护范围不仅包括奥地利（Austria），还远及下游的斯洛文尼亚（Slovenia）和克罗地亚（Croatia），共三个国家。

(5) 题目 18：a country which has partly destroyed one of its most typical features in order to control water （一个国家为治水而部分破坏其最典型国土特征之一）
答案：E
解析：E段讲到以堤坝闻名的荷兰（Dutch），现在却允许工程师“punch holes in dykes”（在堤坝上打洞），这正是破坏其典型特征的行为。

(6) 题目 19：the writer's comment on the comparative cost-effectiveness of traditional flood control and newer methods （作者对传统防洪与新方法成本效益的比较性评论）
答案：G
解析：G段末尾评论道：“It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities... and how little this method achieves.”，通过对比新旧方法的投入与产出，明确评论了其成本效益。

items.text:
（1）题目 20：According to the article, which TWO of these statements are true of the new approach to flood control? （根据文章，关于防洪新方法的哪两项陈述是正确的？）
答案：A（It is designed to slow down the flow of water into the sea. 它旨在减缓水流入海的速度）
解析：B段提到新方法旨在通过"dispersing it... reviving river bends and marshes to curb the flow"（分散水流、恢复河湾和沼泽来遏制水流），这些都是减慢水流速度的措施。

（2）题目 21：According to the article, which TWO of these statements are true of the new approach to flood control? （根据文章，关于防洪新方法的哪两项陈述是正确的？）
答案：D（It will involve the loss/surrender of some land. 它将导致部分土地的损失/出让）
解析：D段和E段都提到了"reflooding"（重新淹没）土地和"return... to its former waterlogged state"（恢复被水淹没的状态），这都意味着将部分土地的使用权还给水。

items.text:
(1) 题目 22：Some of the most severe floods for many centuries have recently occurred in parts of \___\___. （近几个世纪最严重的洪水之一最近发生在哪一地区）
答案：central Europe
解析：A段首句直接提到“winter floods on the rivers of central Europe have been among the worst for 600 to 700 years”。

(2) 题目 23：The Rhine and the \___\___ river have experienced similar problems with water control. （莱茵河与哪条河经历了类似的治水问题）
答案：Mississippi
解析：C段在描述了莱茵河的问题后，紧接着说“The same thing has happened in the US on the Mississippi River...”。

(3) 题目 24：An area near Oxford will be flooded to protect the city of \___\___. （牛津附近的一个地区将被蓄/淹以保护哪座城市）
答案：London
解析：D段提到“To help keep London's feet dry, the UK Environment Agency is reflooding... outside Oxford.”。

(4) 题目 25：Planners who wish to allow water to pass more freely through city surfaces are called \___\___. （允许城市表面更自由渗水的规划者被称作什么）
答案：soft engineers
解析：F段提到“A new breed of ‘soft engineers’ wants cities to be porous...”。

(5) 题目 26：A proposal for part of the city of \___\___ could show whether small-scale water projects could be applied on a large scale. （哪座城市的一个片区提案可检验小尺度项目能否大规模应用）
答案：Los Angeles
解析：G段明确指出“The test case could be Los Angeles... a new scheme... in the Sun Valley section of the city.”，即以洛杉矶的一个片区作为检验大规模应用可能性的试点。
